site: Every form that asks for a consent or preference (Palantir/Lever, Datadog/Greenhouse, Stripe, Cloudflare ...)
class: Each new kind of consent or preference question was a gap in the agent, left blank for the owner on every form, because the answers lived as code per kind (a text-message regex here, a privacy rule there) and not as the owner's standing decisions
symptom: On Palantir, 'AI notetakers ... Yes, I consent / No' and 'share my resume with external partners' were left blank, and 'share my resume' was even matched to the resume-upload concept; on Datadog 'In what cities are you available to work?' stopped an application.
root_cause: No concept existed for these questions, and the owner had never been asked for a standing decision on them, so each form was a fresh question for the owner. The safety classifier also flags the notetaker text as a legal-status question (a false positive in safety.py, reported to the owner, not changed).
why_tests_missed: Tests covered the consent kinds that had already been coded (text messages, privacy notices); nothing exercised a consent kind the code had not seen, and the replay corpus only shows pages after a failure.
fix: Four concepts in reference/concepts.json (AI_NOTETAKER_CONSENT, SHARE_DATA_WITH_PARTNERS, MARKETING_OPT_IN, AVAILABLE_WORK_LOCATIONS), each answered from a profile field the owner sets once (empty = the question comes to the owner, never guessed). Data concepts already win ties over the code table, so the share-my-resume wording no longer becomes a resume upload. Owner decisions of 23 October 2026: notetaker Yes, share with partners No, marketing and talent community No, and the places available to work. Replay of 721 saved pages: 8 pages differ, all corrections (Datadog's cities question and Palantir's two consents).
prevention: Treat an owner's consent and preference decisions as data (a profile setting plus wordings in a data file), asked for once and applied in any wording; find the next unknown wordings by reading questions ahead of time from the portals' public question lists, not by waiting for applications to stop.
